evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
external: https://wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Damage_modifier (live wiki, general game rule only — no repo state)

scope_limitation.statement: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' lives outside the permitted export (scripts/ or tests/), and data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json does not contain it. I therefore could not recompute the absolute raw damage of event 62 from champion base stats. The independent computation below is pinned at the ratio level: which multiplier the golden change applied, and whether that multiplier is the one the cached wiki text and the game's modifier-composition rule require.
scope_limitation.why_this_is_still_decisive: Both candidate values share the same underlying raw damage instance; only the modifier stack differs. The implied multiplier is uniquely determined by the two printed values to within their 0.1 rounding, and the sourced candidate multipliers are far enough apart (1.08, 1.134, 1.16, 1.1664) that only one survives.

sources.source: data/items.json — item 3877 Bloodsong, passives[0] 'Spellblade', branches[0] (cached League Wiki text)
sources.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources.reading: Expose Weakness is a damage-RECEIVED modifier on the target: +8% (melee wielder) / +5% (ranged wielder) from ALL sources, i.e. it amplifies every roster member's damage on the exposed target, not only the item holder's.

sources.source: data/items.json — {{rd|...}} template ordering, cross-checked inside the same cache
sources.quote: Tiamat / Ravenous Hydra / Stridebreaker Cleave: 'deal {{as|{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}|ad}}'; Serpent's Fang: 'reducing any shields they gain within the duration by {{rd|50%|35%}}'
sources.reading: {{rd|X|Y}} = X for melee, Y for ranged (Tiamat Cleave is 40% AD melee / 20% AD ranged; Serpent's Fang venom is 50% melee / 35% ranged). So Bloodsong's Expose Weakness on a melee wielder — the wielder class a Black Cleaver build implies — is the 8% branch, not 5%.

sources.source: data/runes.json — keystone 'Press the Attack', description + effects.damage_amp_ratio
sources.quote: The third stack consumes all stacks to deal ... '''bonus''' adaptive damage and grant you 8% increased damage against champions until 5 seconds after exiting combat with them.  |  "damage_amp_ratio": 0.08
sources.reading: Press the Attack is a damage-DEALT modifier of exactly 0.08, carried as a first-class number in the cache (the only rune in data/runes.json with a damage_amp_ratio).

sources.source: data/items.json — item 3071 Black Cleaver, passive 'Carve', branches[0]
sources.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources.reading: Carve is percentage armor REDUCTION on the target (max 30%), i.e. also a target-side debuff every attacker benefits from — not a wielder-only effect.

sources.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)          (apply_resistance, resistance.py)  ...  R_final = max(0, (R − r_flat)·(1 − r_pct/100)·(1 − p) − f)
sources.reading: Mitigation is linear in raw damage for fixed R (§1.2: 'the mitigation operator x ↦ x·100/(100+R) is linear in raw damage'), so a pure modifier change scales the printed event damage by exactly the product of the modifiers.

sources.source: League of Legends Wiki, 'Damage modifier' (live, fetched 2026-08-13) — general game rule, not repo state
sources.quote: Undocumented: Modifiers to damage dealt now stack additively instead of multiplicatively. Note: Modifiers to damage received still stack multiplicatively. (V26.09 patch history)  |  'All damage modifiers stack additively' (damage dealt section)  |  'Damage reduction from armor and magic resistance and from any other sources stack multiplicatively.'
sources.reading: The wiki keeps two distinct categories and lists our two effects in different ones: Bloodsong under 'Increasing damage received', Press the Attack under 'Increasing damage dealt'. Additivity is stated WITHIN the damage-dealt category only; the dealt group and the received group are separate factors in the damage formula and therefore multiply with each other. The cached data is patch 16.15 (item icon URLs: raw.communitydragon.org/16.15/...), i.e. after V26.09, so the additive-within-dealt rule is the one in force.

step_1_implied_multiplier.note: Because mitigation is linear in raw damage (S5), the golden change is exactly one multiplicative factor on an otherwise unchanged damage instance.

step_2_candidate_multipliers_from_source.model: PtA 8% + Expose Weakness 8% composed ADDITIVELY across categories (1 + 0.08 + 0.08)
PtA 8% (damage dealt) x Expose Weakness 8% (damage received), composed MULTIPLICATIVELY across categories per S6
Alternative: Carve 30% armor reduction (S4) newly applied to this event, target armor A, factor (100+A)/(100+0.7A) per S5

independent_computation.step_3_conclusion: Two source-grounded models land on 109.8 and every model that lands on 94.1-plus-nothing, 101.6, 106.7 or 109.2 is excluded by the printed values. Both surviving models are the same kind of correction — a target-side debuff/amplifier that the roster event should carry (Expose Weakness explicitly reads 'from all sources'; Carve is armor reduction on the target) being composed by the game's own rule. The independently computed value for the leaf is therefore 109.8 (109.76 before display rounding under the 1.08 x 1.08 reading; 109.80 under the Carve reading).
arithmetic: 94.1 x 1.1664    = 109.758  -> 109.8   <-- matches the new golden value
109.8 / 1.1664   = 94.14    -> consistent with the old value 94.1 being the unmodified instance
unrounded-base check: base in [94.05, 94.15] => base x 1.1664 in [109.700, 109.817], which contains 109.8

why_not_old_value_correct: 94.1 corresponds to the damage instance carrying NO amplifier at all. Expose Weakness is written 'increased damage from all sources' (S1) and Carve is armor reduction on the target (S4); both are target-side debuffs in a coupled roster fight, so an event landing on the debuffed target must carry them. There is no sourced reading under which the un-amplified number is the correct one.
why_not_both_wrong: The single sourced way to get 'both wrong' is if the engine double-counted ONE 8% modifier (charging Bloodsong's 8% as both a dealt and a received modifier), in which case the correct value would be 94.1 x 1.08 = 101.6. I disfavour this: the cache carries two independent 8% modifiers in the two different wiki categories (Bloodsong Expose Weakness under 'increasing damage received', Press the Attack damage_amp_ratio 0.08 under 'increasing damage dealt'), the melee 8% branch is the correct branch for a Black Cleaver wielder (S2), and the second surviving model (Carve at armor ~91) reaches 109.8 with no amplifier double-count at all. I flag it as the residual uncertainty rather than hiding it.
residual_uncertainty: I could not read the scenario definition, so I could not verify which champion holds Bloodsong (melee 8% vs ranged 5% branch), whether Press the Attack is the roster keystone, or the target's armor. The verdict rests on the implied multiplier matching a sourced composition and on the direction of the correction, not on a from-scratch absolute recomputation.

S6 (the dealt-additive / received-multiplicative rule) comes from the live wiki, since data/wiki/ holds only an article index (titles + pageids), no wikitext. data/ contains no cached statement of the modifier-composition rule.
